breath_text: Pediatric PDs feel a heavy moral duty to call graduates practice-ready but define readiness differently, just as the ABP moves to EPA-based attestations in 2028. On the way in, pediatrics-specific signals (the NBME shelf, clerkship honors, GHHS) modestly predict early Milestones. Once residents arrive, the hidden struggles are about adapting to the workplace, and Academic Pediatrics shows how help-seeking and autonomy develop along the way.
in_this_issue: What PDs wish they knew at handover

top.headline: "Readiness for what?" How pediatric PDs decide a graduate is practice-ready
bullets: In a grounded theory study, 15 pediatric PDs described an "immense moral responsibility" for the practice-readiness call.
Definitions split three ways: ready as a general pediatrician regardless of career plans, ready for the specific setting the resident is headed to, or ready for fellowship.
top.tip: the ABP moves to EPA-based readiness attestations in 2028. Programs and CCCs need a shared answer to "ready for what?" before then.
top.citation: "Program Directors' Varied Conceptions of Practice Readiness." Pediatrics. Online Sept 2, 2026. PMID 42680169. doi:10.1542/peds.2026-077198

top.headline: Screening season: what actually predicts pediatric intern performance?
bullets: ERAS metrics (518 residents, 10 programs): GHHS (B=0.15, P=.009) and Step 2 CK (B=0.06, P=.007) were associated with overall Milestone performance.

Medical school metrics (414 graduates, 5 sites; Milestones for 228): the NBME Pediatrics shelf was the only factor tied to all 6 competencies, and peds clerkship honors predicted Professionalism and Patient Care.
top.tip: effects are small, and Milestone data were missing for about 45% of graduates in the second study. Use these as nudges in holistic review, not cutoffs.
top.citation: J Grad Med Educ. Aug 2026. doi:10.4300/jgme-d-25-00854.1 and doi:10.4300/jgme-d-25-01139.1

top.headline: The "unknowable" intern: what PDs wish they'd known at handover
bullets: 19 PDs across FM, IM, OB, peds, and surgery shared 38 stories of residents who struggled. The surprises were usually workplace adaptation, not knowledge.
Three kinds of information gaps: known but ambiguous, knowable but absent, and currently unknowable until the resident arrives.
top.tip: add adaptation signals (asking for help, workflow, team integration) to your early-intern check-ins.
top.citation: Bowen JL, Cooper DM, Larson RW, et al. Acad Med. 2026;101(10):1289-96. doi:10.1093/acamed/wvag120

news.text: The ACGME proposes a 43% cut to its Common Program Requirements. The GMEC would approve PD appointments, and the 3-year PD experience minimum would go. New well-being rules: safe options for residents too fatigued to drive home, protected lactation time, and schedule changes during pregnancy. Target date: July 2028.

acadpeds.text: "Do I Need Help?" Interns on night float. In 19 stories from 12 interns, help-seeking fell into three patterns: need help now, do I need help?, and should wait. Acuity and uncertainty sped up calls; not wanting to bother the supervisor slowed them.
Autonomy grows up. 14 PHM fellows followed for 3 years into attending practice moved from "complete independence" to a collaborative model of autonomy.
POCUS for community pediatricians. A year after a 2-day course plus 4 supervised shifts, 44% of 52 respondents used POCUS weekly. Device access drove ongoing use.

quick.text: SAFE-DC: a rounds format (Summary, Active issues, Follow-up, Exit, Drugs/devices, Counseling) for supervising discharge plans. Katz S, et al. Acad Med 2026;101(10):1222.

GPT-4o tutors: struggling first-year students (87 users vs 206 non-users) closed an exam gap, and failures among users fell from 24.1% to 4.4%. Self-selected users. Sami A, et al. Acad Med 2026;101(10):1265.
GME Program Scorecard: a 17-metric dashboard built from existing data took 2,920 analyst hours and $1,600 in licenses; 61% of potential users accessed it. JGME Aug 2026.
LLMs to summarize resident assessment comments. JGME Aug 2026. Title only; the abstract request was rate-limited.
